entities.summary:
William Carlos Williams was an American-Puerto Rican poet and physician closely associated with modernism and imagism. His Spring and All (1923) was written in the wake of T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land (1922). In his five-volume poem Paterson (1946–1958), he took Paterson, New Jersey as "my 'case' to work up. It called for a poetry such as I did not know, it was my duty to discover or make such a context on the 'thought.'" Some of his best known poems, "This Is Just to Say" and "The Red Wheelbarrow", are reflections on the everyday.

William Carlos Williams was a journalists & chroniclers from Rutherford (1883-09-17, Rutherford–1963-03-04). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in modernist poetry and a physician who wrote about everyday life, Williams' work influenced generations of poets and continues to be studied for its innovative style and themes. His poetry also reflected the cultural and social changes of his time.
